newsitem.title: USA: IBM reports solid second quarter results.
newsitem.headline: IBM reports solid second quarter results.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. Monday reported slightly higher earnings for the second quarter, as strong demand for services, semiconductors and disk drives offset declining sales in some hardware lines.
The world's largest computer maker said it earned $1.4 billion, or $1.46 a share, in the quarter, up from $1.3 billion, or $1.26 a share, a year earlier, adjusted for a two-for-one stock split.
The results came slightly above Wall Street's expectations, but not enough to spark a rally in IBM shares, which often have a big influence on the broader stock market.

"On its face it looks like a decent number," one trader said after the report. "But I'm not sure it's going to be enough to drive the stock from here. I think you would have needed a better number for that."

IBM stock fell 75 cents to $103.75 in consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading. It reported results after the close of trading. Analysts had forecast earnings of $1.42 a share on average, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates.

"It was a relatively dull quarter compared to some previous quarters," said Steve Milunovich, a Morgan Stanley analyst. "I don't think it was a very surprising quarter." He said he would not make big changes in his forecasts based on the results or comments from company officials.
Sales rose 4 percent to $18.9 billion from $18.2 billion.

"These results show the ongoing strength of our broad business portfolio," Chairman Louis Gerstner said. "We saw very good customer response to our new System/390 servers and continuing strength in services and hard disk drives."

IBM said strong results in some businesses -- such as semiconductors, services and the disk drives -- as well as improved results in mainframes, offset lower revenue in other segments, such as AS/400 minicomputers, RS/6000 workstations and personal computers aimed at consumers.
IBM said response to its new mainframe models, a traditional source of strength, was good.
IBM also said results from its commercial PCs and PC servers was good. Servers are machines that serve as host computers in networks.
IBM's interim chief financial officer, Lawrence Ricciardi, said he was pleased with the results and the outlook for the rest of the year.
"We are performing in line with our long-term objectives," Ricciardi told Wall Street analysts in a conference call.

Revenue in North America grew 10 percent to $8.6 billion, Asia-Pacific revenue rose 4 percent to $3.8 billion and Latin America grew 8 percent to $847 million. Revenues from Europe, the Middle East and Africa fell 5 percent to $5.7 billion.
Total hardware sales were flat at $8.6 billion.
Services revenues jumped 24 percent to $4.6 billion. About $3.3 billion in new services contracts were signed in the quarter as the business continued to show strong growth.
